tonight.headline: Down 22.6 before kickoff. Check two inactives at 09:30
body: Christian Watson's 22.6 from Thursday is all Footballers have. ESPN projects you 134.4 to their 128.6, a 53% chance. Your lineup as set is the projection lineup.

Warren and Coker are questionable and both expected to play (CBS, SI this morning). This brief runs before inactives: at 09:30 Mexico City, check both. If either is out, the matching card below is the swap.

case.label: Their tight end
case.body: Brock Bowers (knee) is questionable; ESPN sources expect him to play against the Saints at 14:25. Footballers carry no other tight end.

case.label: Their receivers
case.body: Malik Nabers is fully cleared for the Giants (Yahoo) and in their flex. Your Likely shares that offence, so a Winston shootout helps both sides.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Warren or Coker inactive and the swap not made — roughly 11-15 points given away. Each card covers one.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: ESPN projects Pineiro 9.4 and McPherson 7.4; Trey Smack (8.7) is on waivers until 30 Sep. Cincinnati play at Pittsburgh with Burrow off the report (FantasyPros).

case.label: Why hold
case.body: Pineiro came in on 23 Sep. A second change to the seat inside a week gains nothing.

case.label: When to act
case.body: After 30 Sep, and only if Pineiro finishes Week 3 outside the top twenty kickers while McPherson finishes top five.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Both project 7.7. Detroit host a Jets offence missing TE Mason Taylor (ESPN); the Vikings visit a Tampa Bay team whose quarterback was ill this week (Heavy).

case.label: Why hold

case.label: When to act
case.body: Only on a real gap after 2 Oct, when the seat's churn window closes.

case.label: What would change it

doNotChase.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
doNotChase.lead: Scored 1.5 on Thursday. A second tight end has no seat.

case.label: Thursday
case.body: 1.5 points at Green Bay (league file). PFF: two catches across three games, with reduced route participation under the new staff — even with Penix throwing for Drake London's 194 yards.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Same structural objection as Schultz: one TE slot, RB/WR flex.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely ruled out. Even then Schultz is the better use of the seat on role.

case.body: Nothing this season.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage. Monangai (RB) and Boston (WR) are the weakest movable players and nobody clears either. Two weeks of data is thin; the answer stands.
